name: Claw Code

surfaces.label: `claw` (Rust crate rusty-claude-cli, workspace 0.1.3): bare `claw` is a line-editor REPL (rustyline-style prompt `> `, not a full-screen TUI); `claw "text"`, `claw prompt ...`, `claw -p ...` and a piped prompt are one-shots where alive means working. Build-from-source only: no release tag or asset exists, so the binary is rust/target/{debug,release}/claw (or a copy on PATH). The release workflow would name the macOS asset claw-macos-arm64, hence the second name. argv[0] is the only thing matched and only its base name is compared: path_contains is deliberately not used, because it is a substring test and `/rust/target/release/claw` is also a prefix of `.../claw-rag-service` (a Qdrant/SQLite RAG server) and of `claw-analog`, so a dev-build path would file the RAG daemon as a Claw Code session. The bare name `claw` is generic and is the only discriminator left (a renamed or PATH copy is matched the same way). Management subcommands and help/version flags are vetoed by exact argument, so a prompt word equal to one of them (`claw status`, `claw config`) would be vetoed too. `--resume` and `resume` are vetoed because they restore a session, run any slash commands and exit; they never start a REPL.

`claw-analog`, a second, minimal binary in the same workspace (crate claw-analog): one task per invocation (`claw-analog -w <dir> "task"` or stdin), a tool loop with an explicit permission mode. One-shot, so alive means working. Sessions are optional, opt-in JSON snapshots written to a path given with --session; not JSONL and not under .claw. Excluded subcommands are its own (doctor, config, complete). The `-h` and `--help` flags are clap's.

working_signals.meaning: the bash tool runs `sh -lc <command>` as a direct child of the claw process (stdin closed), and hook commands also run as `sh -lc` (stdin piped, not closed); both exist only while a turn is executing a tool or a hook. Tools that are not shells (file read/write, web, grep) run in-process and show no child. macOS /bin/sh may exec a lone simple command in place, in which case the direct child is the command, not sh (inferred, README case 9)

the user prompt is appended when the turn starts, the assistant message only after its stream has ended, and each tool_result right after its tool; a long model stream or a long tool call leaves the file quiet, so this raises working and its absence proves nothing. The file is found by process cwd (newest *.jsonl in the fingerprint directory), not by session id, because a REPL has no id in argv
fallback, unmeasured guess. The agent runs in-process (reqwest/tokio streaming plus terminal rendering), so a model call waiting on the network burns almost nothing

waiting_signals.meaning: no hook, file, socket or event marks a permission wait. The REPL prints 'Permission approval required' ... 'Approve this tool call? [y/N]:' to stdout and blocks on stdin; the transcript then ends on an assistant tool_use record with no tool_result, which looks the same as a slow tool. The .claw/worker-state.json file has a tool_permission_required status but is written only for workers created through the model-facing Worker* tools, not by the REPL itself

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry dependency or OTEL_* variable anywhere in the source. A crates/telemetry crate has a JSONL sink and a SessionTracer (turn_started, tool_execution_started, turn_completed and so on), but nothing in the CLI constructs a tracer or sink outside tests, so no telemetry is written at all

sources.claim: bare `claw` starts the REPL only when stdin is a TTY; a prompt argument, `prompt`, `-p`, or piped stdin make it a one-shot; the REPL uses a line editor with prompt `> `

sources.claim: `--resume` never starts a live session: it loads the session, runs the slash commands given, prints and exits
sources.evidence: main.rs parse_resume_args (~3338) returns CliAction::ResumeSession; resume_session (~5020) with no commands prints 'Restored session from <path> (<n> messages).' and returns. So argv never carries the session id of a running REPL, and session_id_args is left out on purpose

notes: Identity confirmed: ultraworkers/claw-code is a Rust CLI agent harness whose binary is `claw`; it is not a fork or wrapper of Claude Code, although it reads CLAUDE.md files and sends `claude-code` as its user-agent app name. Not installed here, no live process was seen, so nothing is verified-locally. A REPL has no session id in argv (`--resume` exits), so map a process to its transcript by the process cwd: the newest *.jsonl in <cwd>/.claw/sessions/<fnv1a64(canonical cwd) as 16 hex>/, and confirm with session_meta.workspace_root. The store is per project directory, not under ~. The strongest working evidence is a shell child (`sh -lc`) of the claw process; between tool calls, during a model stream, and during a permission wait no signal is exact, so idle must tolerate a short hold window. There is no sleep inhibitor, no waiting record and no OTel. Other harnesses named in the README (LazyCodex, Gajae-Code, oh-my-codex/OmX, clawhip) are separate projects, not surfaces of this row.
